Official GRU4Rec shares candidate columns across the minibatch: other transitions’ targets plus `n_sample` additional draws, nominally K=B−1+n_sample negatives per transition. Additional sampling uses replacement, proportional to frequency^sample_alpha; duplicates remain, and only the diagonal target column is excluded by BPR-max. Thus repeated negatives receive multiplicity weight, and target collisions can remain elsewhere. Independent per-transition sampling changes coverage and gradient correlation; deduplication changes the objective. BPR-max is −log Σⱼwⱼσ(s₊−sⱼ)+λΣⱼwⱼsⱼ², w=softmax over negative scores. The regularizer penalizes scores, not parameters. [Official implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/master/gru4rec.py)

Algebraically, with exactly one valid negative, λ=0, identical scores and no correction/smoothing, BPR-max = BPR = two-candidate softmax cross-entropy = softplus(s₋−s₊), apart from numerical epsilon and constant/reduction conventions. Therefore K=1 cannot test hard-negative weighting. Match loss reductions: current official BPR sums pairwise terms. Activation also matters: BPR-max commonly uses linear or ELU scores, whereas official cross-entropy applies softmax to logits; ELU versus linear changes optimization despite preserving ranking. Cross-entropy’s recommended `logq=1` introduces another difference. [Official guidance](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec)

The paper’s Figure 2 compares gradients with minibatch size 32 and zero versus 2048 additional negatives; Figure 3 includes 0, 32 and 128 additional samples, not total negatives. These are published small-pool references, not fully isolated loss ablations. Proposed controlled experiment: K=4,16,64; identical candidate tensors, sampling distribution, collision policy, score activation, reductions and training schedule; compare BPR, unregularized BPR-max and uncorrected sampled cross-entropy, then vary score regularization and sampling separately. [Original paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf)
